title: 特朗普政府下架 Tetris 克隆游戏 Build The Wall，版权方曾警告严肃对待侵权
content:
White House axes its Tetris clone after copyright warning
Business
PC
Marketing
News
Trump Administration takes down Tetris clone after company warns it takes copyright violation 'very seriously'
Build The Wall has been knocked down.
Bryant Francis
,
Senior Editor
,
GameDeveloper.com
September 9, 2026
3 Min Read
Image by Jakub Rupa via Adobe Stock.
The Trump administration's
promise
to promote its domestic and foreign policy agendas using video game iconography seems to have hit hit an (L-shaped) speed bump. On September 4, 2026, the White House added a new "Arcade" section to its website with five browser games themed around different policy pushes, each mechanically similar to existing games like
Snake
,
Flappy Bird
, and
Tetris
.
Now news outlet
VGC
has spotted that one of those games, a
Tetris
clone called
Build the Wall
, has already been taken down. The game in question was themed around President Trump's
decade-long push
for a physical border wall along the US' southern border that would forcibly block undocumented immigration.
This removal took place days after the
Tetris
copyright holder The Tetris Company
posted a message on social media
disavowing the game and promising that it takes copyright infringement "very seriously."
"At Tetris we believe in the power of connection and bringing people together, not dividing them," the company stated. "To our fans everywhere: we love you, we see you, and we're grateful to have you in our community."
Related:
Riot Games is considering making premium titles, says co-founder
It was in the comments of this post—also dated on September 4—that the company directly commented on
Build the Wall
. "P.S. The Tetris Company was not involved in the creation of
Build the Wall
," it continued. "P.P.S. We take copyright infringement very seriously." The Tetris Company is the first video game industry company to directly criticize the Trump administration's use of its intellectual property in its propaganda—and see its iconography removed in the days after.
Previous social media posts featuring iconography from games like Pokémon or Halo were met with either
pointed distancing
or silence by their property owners. The administration has faced sharper criticism by artists and companies in other mediums, with musicians like
Taylor Swift
and
Bad Bunny
successfully pressing for their songs to be removed from posts promoting its deportation agenda.
It's unknown at this time if The Tetris Company's post—or any follow-up messages to the White House by the Tetris Company—were what prompted the game's removal.
Build the Wall
and
Snake
clone
Rio Run
were
criticized
as promoting racist depictions of undocumented immigrants from Central and South America. In
Rio Run
, players maneuver an anonymous government official across a board, gathering non-white characters that are placed in orange jumpsuits that become the "tail" of the digital snake.
Meanwhile
Build the Wall
modified
Tetris
' core mechanics by adding alien invaders that attempt to breach the assembled falling blocks. These otherworldly enemies are linked to the Trump administration's aggressive—often
violent
—deportation campaign by way of the term "alien," which the
Immigration and Nationality Act
defines as "any person not a citizen or national of the United States." The administration
regularly
refers to undocumented immigrants as "illegal aliens."
Related:
Report: EA is using genAI for commentator voiceover in NHL 27
Ironically it may have been
Build the Wall
's own design logic that undermined its intended message. As
Kotaku
observed before the game was taken down,
Build the Wall
removed the typical
Tetris
mechanic of having the falling blocks vanish when assembled in a perfect straight line, but still flashes a "game over" screen after the bricks reach the top of the screen.
In other words, no matter how high players built the wall, it was impossible to win.
Game Developer has reached out to The Tetris Company for comment and will update this story when the company responds.
